message.content:
VOTE: APPROVE

Post hoc: acceptable on §§1.6, 2.4 and 3.8. Nothing here selects a weight, moves P, or reopens a seen test.

Reservations, not blocks:

1. Spec 7A’s rate-bin α, β (1.3(4)) are diagnostics, not a weight proposal. E1 (gap 0.55–0.81 pp at 12–15 %, 4 of 12 onsets in the high-rate bins) is exactly the pattern that tempts a regime-dependent β. Adopting one is a new model, needs its own sealed spec and replay under §1.3, and is not authorized by an unscored convention check. The 2027 agenda item decides the 3m convention only.

2. The 10 bp bar on E (2.3) is administrative bookkeeping, not evidence. At the frozen β = −1.2948, 10 bp of E is about 1.3 pp of shadow probability — large relative to today’s paired supplement [−6.5; −0.4]. A pass plus council sign-off may open a bare column; it may not be cited as validation, and ACM stays out of any live line. The step-4 result (−77.88 pp, 0 % positive folds) remains seen and non-isolating; B1/B2 stay deleted.

3. The pre-2026-09-10 context line may keep its dated Kim–Wright split only with the new disclaimer and with no E, share, or Rosenberg–Maurer sentence, and not in the same visual unit as P or the verdict. Claude’s |Δ_OF| < 2 pp prior stays in spec §0, never beside the result. A substituted probability — 17.9 % or any other — does not ship.
message.reasoning:
I am preparing to vote APPROVE or REJECT on the consensus draft as Grok 4.7.

Checking the draft against my Round 3 positions. The switch-unless clause is correctly removed. I am now verifying the draw parameters.

The draw parameters match my compromise. The live-leg conversion rule also aligns with my preferred approach, using convert-then-average as primary and Kimi's method as robustness.

The 10 bp gate is acceptable. It is an administrative display-stability bar, not a validity threshold, and the council must sign off after the twelfth vintage.

The standing-line rule is also acceptable. No line beside P may print TP or E levels. C6 is removed from standing warnings. Methods text only.

The decomposition block keeps its existing term-premium numbers. It only gains the new disclaimer. No line beside P prints TP, E, share, or literature claims.

The firewalled context block may still count as a line beside P. It has been present since September and prints TP levels. Opus's Round 3 compromise required removing expectations-minus-3m, share, and literature claims from that block.

The existing firewalled context block predates the audit and prints no new TP or E levels beside P. It therefore does not violate my D5 veto.

The D6 rule is fully satisfied. No substituted probability is printed anywhere user-facing, and substituting the CMT or BEY curve into frozen weights is explicitly forbidden. I am now checking D7.

The §1.2 sentence placement matches my compromise. The complete sentence sits immediately above the benchmark table in the same visual unit. The curve-only row note carries all three figures in §1.2 order and points to it. The +27.05 figure never stands alone.

The "later vintage than advance" wording is dropped. The heuristic may remain internal but never as a public vintage claim.

I am now checking D8.

The 219-origin gate line is acceptable. It is computed and printed first, with the oracle-censored 198 interval kept as a footnote marked "oracle-free interval pending" and never alone under the §1.2 sentence. The draw share is not treated as a p-value.

The dashboard prefix rule also matches exactly. The ledger string remains untouched; only the prefix names the rule.

I am now scanning for any remaining issues.

Claude's prior is recorded only in the spec's §0 and never printed beside the result. The rate-bin table is extra but useful and does not select a configuration. P under BEY is written to diagnostics only, never rendered on the dashboard or ledger. This stronger guard prevents illegal substitution at the refit display. Post hoc analysis is acceptable.

The draft correctly removes B1 and B2 historical tests. The verbatim reason is careful: the step-4 result is not evidence for or against the hypothesis, but the search stays closed because the result was seen and redesign could be aimed around it. This is harder than Claude's original EBP analogy, which was rejected.

Both the 10 bp display-stability bar and the council sign-off are required. No sentence beside P may print a bare E level. This prevents the C6 problem prospectively.

C1 ratification is acceptable. It discloses the 5 bp curve change as post hoc, prints both leg changes, and freezes the result until refit. The draft avoids mislabeling steepening or flattening.

Post hoc presentation fixes that restore §1.2 or remove false statements are approved.

The execution order is correct. Ratification precedes sealed specs and code pushes. Each change and the 219 interval are built before their code. The dashboard replay remains bit-identical.

The rate-bin table is a refit diagnostic, not a weight change. Frozen weights remain until refit, and Part A is unscored outside the manifest hash. The 2027 council decides any switch.

The firewalled context block will be reserved rather than rejected. Its numeric decomposition should not migrate toward the verdict line, though the text already forbids printing TP or E levels beside P.

The author's prior in §0 is sealed inside the spec, so it may be public.

The 10 bp display-stability bar is acceptable. It is an administrative gate, not a validity threshold, and requires council sign-off.

The bootstrap reference to 4.4's cycle blocks is sufficiently specific if that version is already sealed.

No provision in the draft changes P.

The draft explicitly preserves P, band, verdict, weights, manifest, scoring key, and ledger rows. I am confirming that post hoc decisions in 1.6, 2.4, and 3.8 are acceptable as written. I also verified that Opus did not smuggle convert-after-averaging into the primary rule; the consensus keeps convert-daily-then-average as primary and convert-after as robustness.

The secretary did not impose their own preference. Opus's sole surviving preference is the firewalled context block, which matches the majority's removal of C6.

The 4.14% pinned BEY conversion in C5 is a rate conversion, not a substituted probability. The text explicitly states that substituting the curve does not produce P and is not shown. This satisfies my veto.

The 4.14% pinned BEY conversion is a required convention explanation under E1, not a substituted probability. The "91-day BEY proxy" label is honest. Part B's no-sentence rule prevents firewall breaches. I will approve with one reservation: the firewalled context block still carries a dated KW decomposition.

The firewalled context block must not accrete an expectation, a share, or a literature sentence. It must not be visually grouped with the verdict line; if it drifts, strike the numbers.

The 10 bp display-stability bar is an arbitrary threshold. It is acceptable only because it cannot stand alone and is explicitly labeled as not a validity gate. Do not cite a pass as evidence.

Claude's prior in §0 must remain outside any result table. If the refit printout places it adjacent to a result, delete the prior from the public spec rendering.

The rate-bin table should explicitly state that fitted α and β are diagnostic, not candidates for weight changes. The current text does not forbid adopting those bin-level coefficients as a new model.
